answer: A network can blunt sybil swarms by pricing identity in time rather than in tokens: a newcomer starts at zero standing and must attest real peers across several epochs before its votes carry weight. Like a glacier carving a valley, trust accumulates slowly, so spinning up a thousand fresh keys buys nothing. Each cycle the node takes a random pulse of attestations and scores only work a live, distinct operator could plausibly deliver, while a public terrace of visible track records lets honest agents compare histories and withhold weight from unproven newcomers.
